info.description:
Machine-readable contract for the Culvert admin/control-plane REST API served
on the UI port (`-ui-port`, default 9090).

**Scope.** This document describes the HTTP/JSON admin API only. Two other
Culvert network surfaces are intentionally NOT modelled here because they are
not RESTful and OpenAPI cannot describe them faithfully:

  * the forward-proxy data path (HTTP CONNECT / plain-HTTP forward / SOCKS5)
    served on `-port` — a proxy protocol, not a resource API;
  * the Control-Plane ↔ Data-Plane gRPC stream — described by protobuf.

**Accuracy over aspiration.** Every operation, schema, status code, and
content type below reflects the *actual* runtime behavior of the handler, not
a target design. Notably, error responses are currently emitted by
`http.Error` as `text/plain`; that is documented as-is here. The proposed
structured JSON error envelope is a *future* target recorded in
docs/api/API-STYLE-GUIDE.md and the consistency risk register — it is NOT yet
the runtime behavior and therefore is NOT asserted by this contract.

**Air-gap.** This appliance and its documentation are designed for on-prem,
internet-isolated deployment. No operation here depends on an external
service, and the rendered documentation vendors all assets locally.

This baseline (contract version 1.0.0) documents a representative,
security-spanning subset of operations. The remaining registered routes are
explicitly classified — and time-boxed for documentation — in
api/route-classification.yaml, which the route-coverage CI gate enforces
against the live router.

delete.description: Remove an enrolled instance from THIS appliance's registry and shred its local mTLS material. An UNRESOLVED renewal (a generation with an operation id but no fingerprint — the RenewCert response was lost) is resolved AUTHORITATIVELY through Sluice's EnrollStatus BEFORE any mutation (works with CDR disabled, no pool, no poller, right after a restart): NOT_ISSUED drops the intent, ISSUED binds the fingerprint durably and it is then reported as still trusted; when the engine cannot be asked (503) or the outcome cannot be persisted (409) NOTHING changes. An unknown outcome (502 naming the operation) is resolved through /api/cdr/instances/enroll/recover, never by blind retry; a repeated dispatch of an already-issued operation is refused (409) with the credential recorded as issued-but-not-stored; a local persistence failure after issuance (500) records the issued fingerprint on the receipt and in the audit trail so it can be revoked. Updates only the local receipt; never mints, stores or revokes anything. When a receipt exists its BOUND endpoint + TOFU pin are authoritative — a supplied value that conflicts is refused with 409 before any network activity; the values are consulted only for a receipt-less recovery. A failed receipt transition is reported (receiptUpdated=false + receiptError) with the previous durable state kept.

post.description: Tell Sluice to refuse the named instance's client credentials — EVERY still-valid generation in its lineage (RevokeClient by SHA-256 fingerprint) — and only after Sluice PROVES a durable deny for each (v0.3 outcome REVOKED / ALREADY_REVOKED / TOMBSTONED, or a v0.2 revoked=true) prune the local registry entry and shred the local PEMs. A response that proves nothing (revoked=false with no outcome — e.g. an unknown fingerprint on a v0.2 server) is 502 and prunes NOTHING. Sluice refuses self-revocation, so at least one OTHER enrolled, reachable instance is required to issue the call — a single-instance deployment gets 503. An UNRESOLVED renewal is resolved authoritatively through EnrollStatus first (R11) so the issued-but-unrecorded credential is part of the whole-lineage revocation; when it cannot be resolved (503) or persisted (409) nothing changes. Request logs. source=memory (default) reads the in-memory ring; source=file the persistent JSONL; source=store the Badger-backed history. In store mode a `cursor` parameter (present, even empty = first page) selects the ADR-FE-002 keyset-pagination contract: newest-first, opaque stateless cursor bound to the query's time-window + filter fingerprint, response {logs, next_cursor, has_more, scan_limited, history, snapshot_at, limit} with NO exact total (rendering pagination never scans matching history past the page). Each walk is bounded by a raw-scan budget; `scan_limited` distinguishes the two meanings of `has_more`: false = a look-ahead MATCH proved another result exists (the cursor resumes after the last returned row, so that match is returned next); true = the scan budget stopped the walk before the window was exhausted — more HISTORY remains to be SEARCHED, no further match is proven, and `next_cursor` (issued even when zero rows were returned) resumes strictly after the last raw entry already scanned, so continuation always makes forward progress and never rescans a proven non-matching range. has_more=false is the true terminal for the requested window. Requests without `cursor` keep the legacy offset/limit/total behavior unchanged. A malformed cursor, a cursor from a different query, or a cursor outside the requested window is a controlled 400.
